_comment: 1.9 The Wild Woods: forage spots (refill every day), dig spots (finds: minerals, fossils, artifacts) and the expedition board. Items live in items.json (cat forage|mineral|fossil|artifact) and their icons are made in scripts/icon-variants.mjs. kind picks the 3D shape of a forage spot. w = weight in its table. See BALANCE.md > Woods. 1.19 The Deep Woods: regions are islands round the glade (at = centre in woods island space, r = radius), each opened by restoring its trail (a restoration room, ids trail_<region>, in `trails`: bundles work like the village square's). An open region adds its own forage spots and one feature: fireflies (night only, from hour `from` to hour `to`), panning (pans a day shared by its spots, `table` of finds) or taps (trees whose sap is ready `hours` after the last collection).

trails.name: The Hollow Bridge
trails.about: The old footbridge to Mossy Hollow has rotted through. Juniper paints there every spring and wants it back: rope, a basket of woodland finds and a good lunch for the crew.

reward.text: Mossy Hollow opens: moss, bluebells, puffballs, wild garlic, elderberries and rare morels, and fireflies to catch at night.

letter.title: The Hollow is open!
letter.body:
Dear {farmer},

I crossed the new bridge at dusk and the whole hollow was full of fireflies. I sat on a log and forgot to paint anything at all.

Go and see for yourself one evening. Bring a jar.

Juniper

trails.name: The Stepping Stones
trails.about: Crystal Creek runs clear over gravel that still has a little gold in it, Old Tom swears. Help him lay new stepping stones and bring waders, and he will show you how to pan.
trails.rebuilds: the stepping stones to Crystal Creek

reward.text: Crystal Creek opens: watercress, river mint, cattails, water lilies and wild strawberries, and six pans a day for gold flakes, agate, jade and river pearls.

letter.title: Gold in the creek
letter.body:
Dear {farmer},

The stepping stones are down and I found a gold flake on the very first pan. Told you so.

There is a pan waiting for you on the bank. Six goes a day is plenty for anyone's back.

Old Tom

trails.name: The Pine Ridge Path
trails.about: Up on Whispering Pines the old trees are tall enough to hear the wind in. Bram wants iron for the steps up the ridge, a hearty breakfast and something warm for the climb.
trails.rebuilds: the ridge path to Whispering Pines

reward.text: Whispering Pines opens: pinecones, chestnuts, lingonberries, pine boletes and sloes, and six old trees to tap for maple sap and pine resin.

letter.title: Up on the ridge
letter.body:
Dear {farmer},

The path is cut and the steps are iron, so they will outlast both of us. It is quiet up there, just the wind in the pines.

I have set taps in six of the old trees. Come back every few hours and the buckets will be full.

Bram

trails.name: The Root Path
trails.about: Past the three trails, an old path winds into the heart of the forest, where the oldest tree in the valley is said to sleep. Hazel remembers picnics under it as a girl. The path is overgrown and the roots have heaved the stones: it needs a little of everything the woods give.
trails.rebuilds: the root path to the Ancient Grove

reward.text: The Ancient Grove opens: acorns, moonflowers and more, and the Elder Oak waiting to wake.

letter.title: The Elder Oak
letter.body:
Dear {farmer},

I walked the root path this morning, slowly, with my stick. The old oak is still there. It is much smaller than I remember, and very tired.

Wren says it can be woken, a little at a time, with gifts from the woods. I think that would be a lovely thing to do, don't you? It will take a long while. Good things do.

With love,
Hazel

critters._comment: 1.20 Woodland Friends. A feeding stump per critter family (in the glade or a region, which must be open). Leave one of its treats on the stump; the family visits during its hours (local time, from-to, may wrap past midnight) and the treat waits until then, never lost. Tap the visitor to say hello: one visit a day per family. Every visitsPerHeart visits is a heart (up to maxHearts); each heart pays heartCoins x hearts. A visit leaves a gift: one of `gifts` (weights), or the family's `rare` gift with chance rareBase + rarePerHeart x hearts (always at the last heart). Visits grow the Foraging skill (stat critter_visits).

families.name: Deer
families.about: A shy doe and her fawn who step out of the trees while the dew is still on the grass.

families.name: Wild rabbits
families.about: A whole warren lives under the hollow's mossy banks. They thump a welcome when they hear you coming.

families.name: Hedgehogs
families.about: Snuffly little wanderers who trundle out of the leaf piles as the light goes golden.

families.name: Foxes
families.about: A clever red fox family by the creek. They love a fish supper, and they love shiny things even more.

families.name: Red squirrels
families.about: Busy, bouncy and always burying something. They chatter at you from the tallest pines.

families.name: Tawny owls
families.about: A pair of owls nesting in a hollow pine. Leave something soft for their nest and they come down to say hoo.

wren._comment: 1.20 Wren the ranger: lives in a cabin in Whispering Pines once its trail is restored (friends only). One field note a day: bring `need` of a woods item for coins (its sell price x coinsMult + bonus) and Foraging XP (stat field_notes). Every gemsEvery notes adds a gem.
wren.name: Wren
hello: Morning! I counted eleven rabbits before breakfast.
Shh, listen. That's a tawny owl, wide awake for once.
The creek fox has been stealing my teaspoons again.
Every critter has a favourite snack. The trick is knowing which.
My notebook is nearly full. Time for a new one!

camp._comment: 1.21 Camping in the glade: pitch the tent from `pitchFrom` o'clock until `pitchTo` (local time, wraps past midnight), sleep, and from `wakeFrom` o'clock the next morning collect a camp morning: `finds` forage from the glade and the open regions, and a `digChance` chance of a dig find too. Once a night. Woods Foraging XP (stat camp_mornings).

weather._comment: 1.21 Woods weather (the farm's weather of the day, Weather.ts). Nothing is ever only found in one weather. rain: every mushroom spot holds something and mushrooms are `mushroomWeight` x likelier. mist: fossils and artifacts in digs, and the rarer pan finds, are `rareMult` x likelier. sunny: berries and flowers are `sunnyWeight` x likelier.

grove._comment: 1.23 The Ancient Grove: the Elder Oak grows in stages. Each stage is a restoration room (ids grove_<stage>, bundles like the trails', minStar 2 = gold-star items only) and opens when the previous stage is finished, `growDays` days have passed since then (the oak grows) and the player has reached `opensAt`. The first stage needs the Root Path (trail_grove). Finished stages switch on `effects` (src/systems/Grove.ts): roots = forage star chances, shoot = extra pans a day, boughs = critter visits a day, canopy = a glowing canopy at night and extra digs; the crown hands out the `finale`.

finale.title: The Elder Oak
finale.body:
Dear {farmer},

We all walked up the root path together last night: Rosa with a cake, Pip with far too many lanterns, Bram, Old Tom, Juniper with her paints, and Wren, who knew every bird in the branches. The Elder Oak was glowing from root to crown.

It has not looked like that in a hundred years, and it is because of you.

Wren found a sapling growing at its foot and says it should live on your farm. It is waiting in your storage. Look after it.

With love from all of us,
Rosa

stages.name: Waking Roots
stages.about: The Elder Oak is asleep, its roots dry and its leaves brown. Water and soft mulch round the roots will wake it.
stages.rebuilds: the roots of the Elder Oak

reward.text: The Elder Oak wakes. Woods forage is likelier to carry silver and gold stars.

letter.title: It moved!
letter.body:
Dear {farmer},

I was painting the grove at sunrise and a little green bud opened on the Elder Oak, right in front of me. I dropped my brush in the moss.

Everything you pick in the woods looks brighter to me now. Maybe the old tree is saying thank you.

Juniper

stages.name: The Green Shoot
stages.about: A green shoot climbs from the old trunk. It wants light, sweetness and the very best the farm can grow.

reward.text: One more pan a day at Crystal Creek: the oak's roots stir up the gravel.

letter.title: Gold in the roots
letter.body:
Dear {farmer},

The creek has been running brighter since the old oak woke. Its roots reach right down to the gravel and stir it up, I reckon. One more pan a day for you, and do not tell anyone else.

Old Tom

stages.name: Spreading Boughs
stages.about: New boughs spread over the grove, full of nooks for the woodland families. Bring nuts and berries to fill them.

reward.text: Critter families come to their stumps twice a day.

letter.title: So many visitors!
letter.body:
Dear {farmer},

The squirrels are living in the Elder Oak now and they told all their friends. I saw the hedgehogs twice today. TWICE. And the owl looked at me.

You have to come and see.

Pip

stages.name: The Glowing Canopy
stages.about: The canopy is full and green. Old stories say the Elder Oak glowed on summer nights. Fireflies and moonflowers might bring that back.

reward.text: The canopy glows every night, and you can dig once more each day in the woods.

letter.title: A light in the woods
letter.body:
Dear {farmer},

I could see the Elder Oak glowing from my forge last night, all the way across the water. Never seen the like.

The ground round it has gone soft, too. I left you a spare spade by the dig spots: one more dig a day.

Bram

stages.name: The Elder Crown
stages.about: One last growth: the crown of the Elder Oak, taller than any tree in the valley. Bring the forest's rarest gifts and a feast for everyone.
stages.rebuilds: the crown of the Elder Oak

reward.text: The Elder Oak is whole: a sapling of it for your own farm, and a letter from the whole valley.

treehouse._comment: 1.27 The Treehouse in Whispering Pines (src/systems/Treehouse.ts): three build stages, then six furnishings, all restoration rooms (ids treehouse_<name>). Stages open in order at their level once the Pines are open; furnishings once the roof is on. The finished treehouse adds `campFinds` to every camp morning; the telescope shows which wild animals are out today in the Wildlife Album.

stages.name: The Platform
stages.about: The biggest pine in Whispering Pines has a perfect fork three storeys up. Bram says a platform will sit in it like a nest, if the timber is good and the rope is strong.
stages.rebuilds: a platform and a ladder in the great pine

reward.text: A platform and a rope ladder up the great pine.

letter.title: Up we go
letter.body:
{farmer},

Platform's up. Ladder's tied. Don't look down. Actually, do: the view is good.

Bram

stages.name: The Cabin
stages.about: A little cabin on the platform: walls of pine, a round window to paint the sunset from, and a door just big enough.

reward.text: A cabin with a round window on the platform.

letter.title: A room in the trees
letter.body:
Dear {farmer},

I sat in the new cabin this evening and watched the light go gold through the round window. It's the best room in the valley and it's yours.

Juniper

stages.name: The Roof
stages.about: A mossy roof with a flag on top, so everyone knows whose treehouse it is.
stages.rebuilds: a mossy roof and a flag

reward.text: The treehouse is finished: furnish it, and camp mornings bring 2 more finds.

furnishings.name: Log Chairs
furnishings.about: Two log chairs to sit on, rubbed smooth with resin.

reward.text: Two log chairs to sit on, rubbed smooth with resin.

furnishings.name: Mushroom Lamp
furnishings.about: A lamp made from a giant puffball, glowing softly at night.

reward.text: A lamp made from a giant puffball, glowing softly at night.

furnishings.name: Hanging Lanterns
furnishings.about: Firefly lanterns strung from the branches.

reward.text: Firefly lanterns strung from the branches.

furnishings.name: Moss Rug
furnishings.about: A soft green rug of woven moss.

reward.text: A soft green rug of woven moss.

furnishings.name: Bookshelf
furnishings.about: A shelf of field guides and storybooks. Hazel brought most of them.

reward.text: A shelf of field guides and storybooks. Hazel brought most of them.

furnishings.about: A brass telescope. From up here you can spot which wild animals are out today.
